raw_response:
I’m an old hand at this, so I won’t do anything too fancy. My land is only 11.9 mu, and at my age I must watch both cash and labor. I still do the wheat-maize rotation on the same fields because that is the steady way here. Wheat feeds the family and brings cash, and maize follows right after, same as we’ve done many years. If I change too much and it goes wrong, I’m the one who suffers. So this year I’ll do mostly what worked before: wheat in early October, enough base fertilizer so the seedlings come up strong, then one topdressing when it starts growing hard in spring. I have well water, but pumping costs money, so I’ll water wheat about three times if the weather is normal, and maize once, maybe twice only if it turns very dry. For maize I won’t delay after wheat harvest, because that window is short. I’ll buy the usual hybrid seed people around here use, put some fertilizer under it, then add more once when the plants are waist high or taller. I’d rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than let the crop turn yellow and lose yield, but I still keep it in round amounts I can afford.
